KeyBank shares warning signs and practical steps for avoiding phishing, fake shopping sites, payment app scams and other holiday fraud

CLEVELAND, Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- As holiday shopping picks up, so do opportunities for scammers.

Consumers shopping online, tracking packages, buying gift cards or donating to charities can encounter increasingly convincing fraud attempts. Scammers are also using artificial intelligence to create fake retail websites, emails, text messages and even AI-generated voices designed to impersonate trusted companies or people.

Knowing what to look for can help consumers recognize potential fraud before they share personal information or send money.

What are the most common holiday shopping scams?

Here are several scams consumers should watch for during the holiday season:

Bank imposter scams. Fraudsters may call, text or email pretending to represent a consumer's bank. They may claim there has been a suspicious transaction or login attempt, then ask for a one-time passcode, login credentials or debit card information. KeyBank will not initiate a call or text asking for your online banking username or password. KeyBank also will not ask a client to send money to themselves using Zelle®, an account transfer or a wire payment, or request remote access to your computer or mobile device. However, in some cases, we will call to verify your identity by asking for a one-time passcode that is sent to your mobile device.

Phishing and smishing scams. Fraudulent emails and text messages can look like legitimate communications from retailers, banks or delivery companies. Scammers may also use AI to create convincing fake retail websites and communications intended to capture debit card, credit card or other personal information. A common example is a fake package-delivery message asking for payment to release or redeliver an order.

Vishing and AI voice scams. Criminals can use AI-generated voices in phone calls to impersonate customer service representatives, delivery companies, family members or others in an effort to obtain sensitive information.

Payment app scams. Consumers should be cautious when an unfamiliar seller asks for payment through Zelle®, Venmo, Cash App, wire transfer or cryptocurrency. Recovering money sent to a fraudulent seller through these methods can be difficult.

Online marketplace scams. Fraudsters may advertise popular holiday gifts at unusually low prices, then request advance payment through a payment app, gift card or cryptocurrency before disappearing.

Gift card scams. Criminals may tamper with gift cards displayed on retail racks or convince victims to provide gift card numbers over the phone to make supposedly urgent payments.

Charity scams. The season of giving can also attract criminals impersonating legitimate charities or disaster-relief organizations through phone calls, texts, emails and social media.

5 ways to shop more safely this holiday season

A few habits can make it harder for scammers to succeed:

  1. Be skeptical of unexpected communications. Don't automatically trust an unsolicited call, email or text, even if it appears legitimate. Avoid clicking unfamiliar links or attachments and independently verify the communication using a known phone number, website or app.
  2. Monitor financial accounts regularly. Reviewing account activity frequently can help consumers identify unauthorized transactions sooner. KeyBank recommends clients check their accounts daily and report unauthorized activity immediately.
  3. Turn on multi-factor authentication. MFA provides another layer of account security by requiring an additional form of verification when signing in.
  4. Use secure internet connections. Avoid conducting financial transactions over public Wi-Fi. A secure Wi-Fi connection or virtual private network, or VPN, can help protect data.
  5. Look for buyer protection. When shopping through online marketplaces, consider platforms offering buyer protections and avoid paying sellers who cannot be independently verified.

Holiday scam warning signs consumers shouldn't ignore

Consumers should pause when they encounter:

  • A deal that seems too good to be true
  • An unexpected call, email or text
  • Pressure to send money or act immediately
  • Requests to keep a transaction secret
  • Requests for passwords, codes or sensitive financial information
  • Demands for payment through gift cards, cryptocurrency or payment apps
  • Last-minute requests to change payment information
  • Requests for remote access to a computer or device

These behaviors can indicate an attempted scam.

What should you do if you think you've been scammed?

Speed matters.

Consumers who believe they have been targeted or have already sent money should contact their financial institution immediately and report suspected fraud to the retailer and appropriate authorities. KeyBank clients can contact the KeyBank Fraud Client Service Center at 1-800-433-0124. Dial 711 for TTY/TRS.

Additional information about emerging scams, account security and fraud prevention is available at key.com/fraud.

Ultimately, one of the strongest defenses against holiday fraud is taking a moment before responding. An unexpected message, urgent request or unusually attractive deal is worth verifying independently before clicking a link, providing information or sending money.

Collaboration will let customers authorize AI agents to pay, transfer and settle in gold, positioning Blue Gold in a market forecast to reach nearly USD 400 billion by 2035

NEW YORK, Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Blue Gold Limited (Nasdaq: BGL, BGLWW) (“Blue Gold” or the “Company”) today announced that it has signed a Memorandum of Understanding with Current Technology (TripleBolt Technology Corporation) (“Current”), an AI-native software and consulting firm, to bring agentic AI payments into Blue Gold’s new gold-powered banking app. Under the collaboration, Blue Gold customers will be able to authorize AI agents to initiate and manage payments, bill pay, transfers and purchases on their behalf, within spending limits and permissions they set and can revoke at any time. Payments are expected to settle in gold or gold-backed balances where available, combining the stability of gold with the speed and convenience of AI-driven commerce.

According to Deloitte, by 2030, agentic commerce could drive up to $17.5 trillion in commerce, making it a pivotal force in the future of payments and consumer engagement.

The payments layer that powers this shift is growing quickly. According to DataM Intelligence, the global agentic payments market was valued at USD 18 million in 2025 and is projected to reach USD 398.99 billion by 2035, a compound annual growth rate of 172%. North America led the market with an estimated 36.8% share in 2025. Growth is driven by AI agents making autonomous purchases, new agentic commerce protocols and payment standards, and rising demand for frictionless, personalized checkout.

“The question isn’t whether agentic payments will transform financial services—it’s whether your organization will lead this transformation or be disrupted by it,” said Kevin Clark, Executive Chairman of Blue Gold. “The infrastructure is being built, the market is expanding rapidly, and early movers are already gaining competitive advantages.”

“Agentic payments are moving from concept to real money movement, and the institutions that build them in now will set the standard,” said Erin Barton, Co-Founder and Chief Operating Officer of Current. “Blue Gold has the gold infrastructure and a clear vision for modern banking. Our job is to deliver agents that customers can trust with their money: clear permissions, strong controls and a full audit trail behind every transaction. We are proud to help Blue Gold bring that to market.”

The collaboration is expected to cover agentic payment experience design, AI agent development, integration with Blue Gold’s banking and gold settlement infrastructure, support for emerging agentic commerce standards, and controls for consent, fraud prevention and compliance. The parties intend to begin with a pilot before a broader rollout.

The Memorandum of Understanding is non-binding with respect to the collaboration, which remains subject to due diligence, the execution of definitive agreements and any required regulatory approvals.

About Blue Gold Limited

Blue Gold Limited (Nasdaq: BGL) is a gold-focused company pursuing opportunities spanning gold mining, trading and financial services. Through its Standard Gold initiative, the Company is developing technology intended to connect physical gold ownership with digital financial services and payment infrastructure.

For further information, visit www.bluegoldltd.com.

About Current Technology

Current Technology (TripleBolt Technology Corporation), headquartered in Portland, Maine, is an AI-native consulting and software delivery firm. Current helps companies put AI to work through agentic consulting, software builds, systems implementations and AI enablement. Learn more at current.inc.

Year-to-date revenue increases 13.4%, gross margin improves to 67.9%, and interest expense declines 90%.

West Palm Beach, FL, Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- QHSLab, Inc. (the “Company”) (OTCQB: USAQ), an SEC-reporting healthcare technology and software-as-a-service (SaaS) company whose annual financial statements are independently audited, today provided a shareholder update regarding its financial performance for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the continued evolution of its business, and management’s operational and strategic priorities as the Company approaches 2027.

Dear Shareholders,

While much of our communication is shaped by SEC reporting requirements, I wanted to take the time to write to you personally and share my perspective on where we are as a business and where we are heading.

Following the filing of our quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the period ended September 30, 2026, I wanted to provide our shareholders with additional perspective on our financial performance, the continued evolution of our business, and management’s priorities as we approach 2027.

During the first nine months of 2026, we continued to make progress in transitioning QHSLab toward a scalable, technology-enabled healthcare services business. While we achieved meaningful growth in our Integrated Service Program (ISP) and improved our gross margins, we also experienced a decline in our allergy diagnostics and immunotherapy business, increased operating expenses and greater demands on our available cash resources.

Year-to-Date 2026 Financial Highlights

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared with the corresponding period in 2025, the Company reported the following unaudited financial results:

  • Total revenue increased 13.4% to $2,253,347, compared with $1,987,931.
  • ISP revenue increased 63.9% to $1,287,692, compared with $785,506.
  • Gross profit increased 15.6% to $1,529,050, compared with $1,322,590.
  • Gross margin improved to 67.9%, compared with 66.5%.
  • Interest expense decreased 90.0% to $19,482, compared with $194,894.
  • Net loss totaled $119,021, compared with a net loss of $99,156.

Continued Growth of Our Integrated Service Program

Our ISP remains the principal driver of revenue growth and an important component of our long-term business strategy.

During the first nine months of 2026, ISP revenue increased by $502,186, representing year-over-year growth of 63.9%. More importantly, ISP now accounts for approximately 57% of our total revenue, compared with approximately 40% during the corresponding period in 2025.

This change in revenue composition reflects the continued evolution of QHSLab toward a software-enabled healthcare services business built around ongoing relationships with medical practices.

During the third quarter of 2026, ISP revenue increased 17.4% year-over-year to $421,792. While the rate of growth moderated compared with the first half of the year, the program continued to expand its contribution to our overall business.

We remain focused on acquiring new medical practice customers, increasing utilization among existing customers, expanding our portfolio of digital healthcare services, and improving the operational efficiency and scalability of our service delivery model.

Allergy Diagnostics and Immunotherapy Treatment

Combined revenue from allergy diagnostic kit sales and immunotherapy treatment decreased 19.3% to $828,854 during the first nine months of 2026, compared with $1,027,611 during the corresponding period in 2025.

The decline was more pronounced during the third quarter, with combined allergy-related revenue decreasing 37.0%, reflecting lower purchasing activity among certain existing physician customers. As a result, despite continued ISP revenue growth, total third-quarter revenue decreased 8.1% to $677,172.

In September 2026, we implemented changes to our supplier arrangements that are expected to reduce the cost of our allergy diagnostic kits by approximately 10% to 13%, based on historical sales volumes and product mix. These changes are intended to improve the profitability of future allergy diagnostic kit sales.

Management remains focused on improving the commercial and financial performance of this established business line.

Gross Margins, Operating Expenses and Profitability

Despite the decline in allergy-related revenue, our overall gross margin improved to 67.9% for the first nine months of 2026, compared with 66.5% during the corresponding period in 2025.

For the nine-month period, gross profit increased by $206,460, or 15.6%, compared with the prior year. However, total operating expenses increased by $401,737, or 32.7%, principally reflecting increased personnel, sales and marketing expenditures, corporate insurance and administrative costs.

Research and development expenditures decreased approximately 5% to $350,604, while we continued to enhance our proprietary technology platform and expand our healthcare service capabilities.

The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into our engineering and software development processes is improving development efficiency, accelerating product enhancements and enabling us to scale our technology platform without a corresponding increase in development expenditures.

We are increasingly realizing the benefits of our historical investments in technology, software architecture and clinical intellectual property. Our existing technology infrastructure and engineering resources are currently sufficient to support our planned platform enhancements, expansion of healthcare service capabilities and growth in customer utilization.

While the full commercial and financial benefits of these developments are not yet reflected in our revenue and earnings, management believes we are establishing a more capital-efficient and scalable business model. Our technology platform is designed to accommodate a substantially larger customer base without requiring proportionate increases in development expenditure.

As we approach 2027, our focus is increasingly shifting toward commercial execution, customer acquisition, utilization and generating financial returns from the technology and operational infrastructure we have established.

We believe this represents an important stage in the evolution of QHSLab as we work toward sustainable profitability and positive operating cash flow.

Management recognizes the need to improve operating leverage by generating additional revenue from the technology, personnel and operational infrastructure already established within the business. Our priority is to translate future revenue growth into improved operating profitability and positive cash flow.

Liquidity and Capital Resources

During the past twelve months, we substantially reduced our outstanding debt obligations and associated financing costs. Interest expense for the first nine months of 2026 declined by approximately $175,000 compared with the corresponding period in 2025.

As of September 30, 2026, the Company reported:

  • Cash and cash equivalents of $190,464.
  • Net accounts receivable of $308,923.
  • Total current assets of $519,108.
  • Total current liabilities of $247,114.
  • Positive working capital of $271,994.
  • No outstanding long-term liabilities.

Total liabilities decreased approximately 54.7%, from $546,078 at December 31, 2025, to $247,114 at September 30, 2026.

Cash decreased by $445,693 during the first nine months of 2026, reflecting approximately $335,000 used in operating activities and $111,000 used in financing activities related to debt repayment. This compares with approximately $80,000 generated from operating activities during the corresponding period in 2025. Operating cash flow during 2026 was impacted by operating losses, increased accounts receivable and a reduction in outstanding accounts payable.

Management remains focused on improving cash collections, managing operating expenditures and increasing the contribution of ongoing service-based revenues to operating cash flow.

While the reduction in debt has lowered financing costs, improving liquidity remains an important priority. As disclosed in our Form 10-Q, substantial doubt remains regarding the Company's ability to continue as a going concern. Our ability to continue operations depends upon achieving sustainable positive operating cash flow or obtaining additional financing, if necessary.

Our objective remains to increasingly support the business through internally generated cash flow.

Management's Focus as We Approach 2027

As we approach 2027, our operational priorities remain clear:

  • Expand our network of medical practice customers and accelerate customer activation.
  • Increase ongoing service revenue through greater utilization of ISP among new and existing customers.
  • Commercialize additional software-enabled healthcare programs using our existing technology infrastructure.
  • Improve the commercial and financial performance of our allergy diagnostics and treatment business.
  • Generate greater operating leverage from our existing technology, personnel and administrative infrastructure.
  • Improve cash collections, expenditure management and operating efficiency.
  • Work toward sustainable operating profitability and positive cash flow.

We believe the progress we have made in developing our technology platform, expanding our healthcare service capabilities and reducing our financing costs provides a foundation for the next stage of our business development.

Management Commentary

“Building a sustainable healthcare technology company requires us to remain focused on the fundamentals of our business. We are encouraged by the continued growth of our Integrated Service Program and its increasing contribution to our overall revenue. At the same time, we recognize that revenue growth alone is not enough. We must translate that growth into improved operating profitability and positive cash flow,” said Troy Grogan, President and Chief Executive Officer of QHSLab.

“Our priorities are to grow revenue, improve the performance of our allergy diagnostics and treatment business, exercise greater discipline over operating expenditures, and generate improved financial returns from the technology and operational infrastructure we have established.

“An important development that may not yet be fully apparent in our financial results is the increasing scalability of our technology and the productivity of our engineering team. We are developing more capabilities, expanding our healthcare service offerings and improving our platform without increasing our research and development expenditures. Our challenge and opportunity now is to translate these capabilities into greater customer adoption, revenue growth and improved earnings. We are focused on building a commercially sustainable healthcare technology business through disciplined investment and responsible capital allocation.”

“We recognize the importance of shareholder value and appreciate the confidence our shareholders have placed in management. While short-term fluctuations in our share price are not within management's direct control, we remain focused on the factors we can influence: the quality of our products and services, customer growth and retention, operating efficiency, responsible capital allocation and financial performance.

“As we approach 2027, our focus is increasingly on converting the progress we have made in building our business into sustainable financial performance. We believe that executing on these fundamentals is the most meaningful way to work toward creating long-term shareholder value.”

On behalf of our entire team, I would like to thank our shareholders for their continued support and interest in QHSLab.

Sincerely,

Troy Grogan
President and Chief Executive Officer
QHSLab, Inc. (OTCQB: USAQ)

Financial results included in this release are unaudited. Shareholders are encouraged to review the Company’s complete quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the period ended September 30, 2026, filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission on November 12, 2026.

For additional information, including the Company’s latest corporate presentation, please visit the QHSLab investor relations website at https://www.qhslab.com/for-investors.

About QHSLab, Inc.

QHSLab, Inc. (OTCQB: USAQ) is an SEC-reporting healthcare technology company focused on improving preventive and value-based care through digital health solutions and point-of-care services. The Company provides healthcare organizations with technology-enabled programs designed to identify patient health risks, support clinical decision-making, improve patient engagement, and create new opportunities for practice revenue.

QHSLab files periodic reports with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, and its annual financial statements are subject to independent audit. The Company is focused on disciplined growth, financial transparency and expanding its portfolio of healthcare solutions for medical practices and their patients.

For more information, visit QHSLab.com.

These statements reflect management’s current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially, including changes in healthcare reimbursement policies, customer adoption and retention, demand for the Company’s products and services, operating expenses, collection of accounts receivable, availability of additional financing and the Company’s ability to achieve sustainable profitability and positive operating cash flow.

Company to contribute Greenlandic project-development experience to selected Nordic forum and undertake separate stakeholder engagement in Nuuk

CHARLOTTE, NC, Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Greenland Mines Ltd (Nasdaq: GRML; FSE: HK6) (“Greenland Mines” or the “Company”) today announced that President Bo Møller Stensgaard has accepted an invitation to join the “Building Nordic Value Chains” panel discussion at the Nordic Forum on Raw Materials (“RAW”) conference, “Strengthening Collaboration on Critical and Strategic Raw Materials,” in Nuuk, Greenland, December 8–10, 2026. Dr. Stensgaard and Robert Møller, the Company’s Nuuk-based Permitting & Community Officer, plan to attend the conference.

Convened through personal invitations, the conference will bring together a selected group of senior representatives and experts from industry, academia, research organisations, public authorities and governments across the Nordic region. Organizers have identified participants based on their experience, expertise, and ability to contribute to a strategic dialogue on the future of Nordic critical and strategic raw-material cooperation.

Greenland Mines views the invitation to contribute to the panel as recognition of the practical perspective it brings through its active development projects, Greenlandic presence, and relationships across the Nordic minerals sector.

Connecting Greenlandic Resources with Nordic Industrial Strength

The conference will examine how closer Nordic cooperation can support research, innovation, investment, skills, and competitive mineral-based value chains. RAW is coordinated by Nordic mining and minerals industry associations and supported by Nordic Innovation, an organization within the Nordic Council of Ministers. Its network connects industry, research, finance, and public-sector stakeholders across the Nordic countries and autonomous regions.

Through the panel discussion, Greenland Mines intends to contribute experience from advancing the Sarfartoq neodymium-praseodymium rare earth project in southwest Greenland and the Skaergaard palladium-platinum-gold project in southeast Greenland. Its focus will be on connecting Greenlandic resources with Nordic expertise and industrial capacity, and on the practical requirements for moving projects forward: technical studies, permitting, environmental understanding, infrastructure, financing, and meaningful local participation.

“The Nordic region has the resources, technical expertise and industrial capabilities to make a much greater contribution to critical-mineral supply security. The challenge is to connect those strengths and translate them into responsible projects and competitive supply chains,” said Bo Møller Stensgaard, President of Greenland Mines.

“The invitation to join the ‘Building Nordic Value Chains’ panel gives us an opportunity to bring a Greenland-focused developer’s perspective to this strategic discussion,” Stensgaard continued. “Our focus is what it takes to move from geological potential and resource development to technically sound, financeable and permitted mining projects - and where Nordic cooperation can make a practical difference.”

Grounded in Greenland, Connected Across the North Atlantic

The Company’s delegation combines project-development leadership with a local perspective. Robert Møller, who is Greenlandic/Inuit and based in Nuuk, brings local knowledge and a focus on permitting and community engagement to the Company’s participation.

Alongside the conference, Greenland Mines is arranging separate meetings in Nuuk with local institutional stakeholders, authorities, and international representatives in Nuuk to discuss the Company’s activities, responsible project development and opportunities for local value creation, and to provide updates on its ongoing international partnership activities.

“Our presence in Nuuk is about more than participating in a conference,” Stensgaard continued. “It is an opportunity to listen, strengthen relationships and discuss how our projects can progress responsibly and create lasting value in Greenland. With Robert based in Nuuk, we bring an ongoing local presence to that dialogue. International expertise and investment must connect with Greenlandic priorities, local communities, businesses and opportunities for people in Greenland.”

The conference’s emphasis on cross-border cooperation aligns with Greenland Mines’ North Atlantic Critical Metals Corridor vision: connecting responsibly developed Greenlandic resources with Nordic and wider allied capabilities in research, technology, logistics, processing, investment and industrial markets.

Sarfartoq and Skaergaard provide complementary foundations for that vision, spanning rare earth magnet materials and palladium, platinum and gold. The Company sees Nordic collaboration as an opportunity to strengthen the technical and commercial relationships needed to advance these projects while supporting potential economic activity in Greenland and the wider North Atlantic.

“Supply security will not be built through isolated projects or policy announcements alone,” Dr. Stensgaard added. “It requires resources, infrastructure, technology, capital and local participation to move together. That is the practical cooperation we want to help build - and why this dialogue in Nuuk matters.”

Participation in the conference, panel discussion and separate stakeholder meetings does not constitute endorsement of Greenland Mines by the organisers, meeting counterparties or participating institutions and does not imply any financing, permitting, commercial agreement or partnership commitment.

About Greenland Mines Ltd

Greenland Mines Ltd is listed on Nasdaq and develops mineral assets in Greenland, including the Skaergaard precious-metals project in southeast Greenland and the Sarfartoq neodymium-praseodymium rare earths project in southwest Greenland. Its North Atlantic Critical Metals Corridor strategy seeks to connect Greenland resources with processing capacity and industrial customers in the United States and allied countries. The Company’s portfolio also includes a strategic investment in AnorTech, which is developing alumina and other materials from Greenland anorthosite.

Water Energy Services transaction broadens Direct Midstream's geographic footprint across four major oil and gas producing regions

Dallas, TX, Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Vivakor, Inc. (Nasdaq: VIVK) ("Vivakor" or the "Company"), an integrated energy infrastructure company providing transportation, terminaling and storage, supply and trading, and environmental solutions, today highlighted Direct Midstream, LLC's ("Direct Midstream") announcement regarding the completion of due diligence and ongoing integration of water infrastructure assets under its agreement with Water Energy Services, LLC.

Vivakor, which recently entered into a definitive agreement to acquire 100% of Direct Midstream, believes the Water Energy Services transaction further enhances the strategic value of the pending acquisition. The transaction encompasses a diversified portfolio of saltwater disposal wells, freshwater and brine facilities, related infrastructure and real property across the Permian Basin, Eagle Ford, East Texas and Barnett Shale producing regions. Certain assets are already included in Direct Midstream's existing infrastructure portfolio, with additional asset transfers underway that are expected to further expand its operating footprint and water management capabilities across Texas.

The transaction complements Direct Midstream's recently announced 52-well operating agreement in Southeast New Mexico and provides strategic alignment with Vivakor's established crude oil logistics, terminaling and environmental services operations across Texas.

"The continued expansion of Direct Midstream's water infrastructure platform further reinforces the strategic rationale behind our planned acquisition," said James Ballengee, Chairman, President and Chief Executive Officer of Vivakor. "The complementary nature of our businesses creates opportunities to leverage our combined infrastructure and commercial relationships, expand our service offerings to existing and prospective customers, and pursue new growth opportunities across some of the nation's most active oil and gas producing regions."

The transfer and integration of certain Water Energy Services assets remain subject to applicable regulatory approvals and other contractual conditions. Vivakor's acquisition of Direct Midstream remains subject to its applicable closing conditions.

Direct Midstream is a provider of midstream energy and fluid management services serving oil and gas operators throughout New Mexico and the Permian Basin. The company’s services include oil production operations, saltwater disposal, produced water management, oil recovery and reclamation, slop oil processing and related oilfield waste services. Direct Midstream utilizes Class II UIC wells, automation and advanced monitoring systems to support safe, efficient and environmentally responsible operations.

For more information, please visit the website: https://directmidstream.com

Vivakor, Inc. is an integrated provider of sustainable energy transportation, storage, reuse, and remediation services. Vivakor’s integrated facilities assets provide crude oil, storage, transportation, reuse, and remediation services under long-term contracts.   • Tiziana reports favorable safety and tolerability profile with intranasal foralumab after 48.1 patient-years cumulative exposure
  • Intranasal foralumab has been well tolerated across all studies, with no serious adverse events related to study drug

BOSTON, Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Tiziana Life Sciences, Ltd. (Nasdaq: TLSA) (“Tiziana” or the “Company”), a biotechnology company developing breakthrough immunomodulation therapies with its lead development candidate, intranasal foralumab, a fully human anti-CD3 monoclonal antibody, today announced the submission of its annual Development Safety Update Report (DSUR) to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA). This DSUR (dated September 2, 2024 to September 30, 2026) reports no drug-related serious adverse events after a cumulative exposure of 48.1 patient-years, highlighting the safety and tolerability data profile of intranasal foralumab in treating neuroinflammatory and neurodegenerative diseases, including non-active secondary progressive multiple sclerosis (na-SPMS), Alzheimer’s disease (AD), multiple system atrophy (MSA), and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS).

“We have seen 48.1 patient-years of cumulative foralumab exposure with no study drug-related serious adverse events, a milestone that reinforces the safety of our intranasal approach,” said Ivor Elrifi, Chief Executive Officer of Tiziana. “Acceptable safety and tolerability continue to be observed across our CNS programs, supporting continued clinical development. We believe that this favorable safety and tolerability profile additionally paves the way for exploring the use of nasal foralumab, not only as a mono-therapy, but also as a multiple sclerosis combination therapy for patients on anti-CD20 approved therapies such as Ocrevus® (ocrelizumab). We have previously announced a memorandum of understanding (MOU) signed with King Abdullah International Medical Research Center (KAIMRC) in Saudi Arabia, with our intention to collaborate on a clinical trial evaluating this combination therapy.”

Key highlights from the submission include:

  • Expanded Access Program (IND 161148): As of 30 September 2026, fourteen (14) patients with na-SPMS were treated with nasal foralumab at Brigham and Women’s Hospital. They received nasal foralumab at 50 or 100 micrograms per dosing day (6 days per three-week cycle) for durations ranging from 23 weeks to 4.7 years. The total cumulative patient exposure in this study is 32.1 patient-years.

  • TILS-021 Randomized Trial and TILS-022 Open-Label Extension: This randomized, double-blind trial in patients with na-SPMS administers foralumab intranasally at doses of either 50 or 100 µg in addition to placebo. The trial completed enrollment (48 patients total) in the summer of 2026, with the last patient dosed on 17 August 2026. Thirty (30) patients were administered foralumab. The total estimated cumulative patient exposure in this study and the open-label extension is 10.25 patient-years.

  • Alzheimer’s Disease (TILS-024 and Expanded Access): Tiziana initiated study TILS-024 in Q4 2025. This randomized, controlled, double-blind study uses a 3:1 treatment ratio (50 µg intranasal foralumab versus placebo) with the same dosing schedule. It is estimated that eleven (11) patients have received nasal foralumab in the reporting period, with an estimated cumulative patient exposure of 1.4 years. One (1) patient with moderate AD continued treatment in a single-patient expanded access IND (IND 172400) at 50 micrograms intranasally per dosing day (6 days per three-week cycle) and has completed 93 weeks of therapy (1.8 total patient-years).

  • Multiple System Atrophy (TILS-025): Initiated in the second half of 2025, this open-label study uses the same dosing schedule. Seven (7) patients have received nasal foralumab for 3–8 weeks duration, with a cumulative patient exposure of 2.50 years.

  • ALS (TILS-ALS-01): Initiated in Q3 2026, this randomized, controlled, double-blind study uses a 3:1 treatment ratio (50 µg intranasal foralumab versus placebo) with the same dosing schedule. It is estimated that two (2) patients have received nasal foralumab in the reporting period, with an estimated cumulative patient exposure of 0.04 years.

In these studies investigating intranasal foralumab in central nervous system (CNS) diseases, favorable safety and tolerability have been observed. During the reporting period, no new risks were identified that resulted in significant protocol amendments for any of the clinical studies. The types and frequency of reported adverse events are generally consistent with those from previous reporting periods.

In conclusion, no substantive changes to the previous knowledge of foralumab safety and tolerability when administered intranasally to patients with CNS disease were identified during the reporting period. The benefit:risk for intranasal foralumab remains favorable in these patients and continued clinical development in CNS patients is warranted. No new actions to address the safety of intranasally delivered foralumab have arisen from the current reporting period.

The cumulative estimated drug exposure for these subjects is 48.1 patient-years. No serious adverse events so far attributed to study drug in nasal foralumab CNS studies. The safety profile of intranasal foralumab aligns with prior studies of foralumab administered intravenously (IV) in healthy volunteers, patients with Crohn’s disease, and kidney transplant recipients. Unlike IV administration, which has been linked to infusion-related reactions seen with other anti-CD3 monoclonal antibodies, nasal delivery of foralumab appears to have better tolerability, with no such issues observed to date.

About Foralumab
Foralumab, a fully human anti-CD3 monoclonal antibody, is a biological drug candidate that has been shown to stimulate T regulatory cells when dosed intranasally. The recently announced INFORM-MS Phase 2a, placebo controlled, double blind trial met its dual primary endpoints for (1) statistically significant reduction (p=0.0168) in microglial activation as measured by TSPO PET imaging in patients treated with 50 ug nasal foralumab as compared to placebo and (2) safety/tolerability. Foralumab treated subjects showed statistically and clinically significant improvements in Modified Fatigue Impact Scale (MFIS) scores compared with their own baseline scores after only 12 weeks of drug therapy. Subjects treated with 50 ug nasal foralumab saw a -6.17 point decrease from baseline (p=0.035), and those treated with 100 ug experienced a -7.18 decrease from baseline (p=0.040). At present, 14 patients with Non-Active Secondary Progressive Multiple Sclerosis (na-SPMS) have been dosed in an open-label intermediate sized Expanded Access (EA) Program (NCT06802328) with either an improvement or stability of disease seen within 6 months in all patients. Intranasal foralumab is also currently being studied in additional Phase 2 trials in Alzheimer’s disease (AD), multiple system atrophy (MSA), and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). Intranasal foralumab is the only fully human anti-CD3 monoclonal antibody (mAb) currently in clinical development. Immunomodulation by intranasal foralumab represents a novel avenue for the treatment of neuroinflammatory and neurodegenerative human diseases.[1],[2]

About Tiziana Life Sciences

Tiziana Life Sciences is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing breakthrough therapies using transformational drug delivery technologies to enable alternative routes of immunotherapy. Tiziana’s innovative intranasal approach has the potential to provide an improvement in efficacy as well as safety and tolerability compared to intravenous (IV) delivery. Tiziana’s lead candidate, intranasal foralumab, which is the only fully human anti-CD3 mAb currently in clinical development, has demonstrated a favorable safety profile and clinical response in patients in studies to date. Tiziana’s technology for alternative routes of immunotherapy has been patented with several applications pending and is expected to allow for broad pipeline applications.

MIAMI, FL / ACCESS Newswire / November 27, 2026 / Sekur Private Data, Inc., a Miami-based Swiss-hosted cybersecurity, private communications, and defense communications company serving enterprise, government, and defense clients, and a wholly owned U.S. subsidiary of Sekur Private Data (OTCQB:SWISF)(CSE:SKUR)(FRA:GDT0) ("Sekur" or the "Company"), today announced that it has deployed a new user interface (UI) for SekurMessenger, its secure team messaging and collaboration platform, incorporating SekurVoice encrypted voice calling directly into the messaging experience. The new UI improves usability and the flow of functions across the application, making SekurMessenger much more user-friendly for the defense, government, enterprise, and executive users who rely on it every day. The Company has received great feedback on the new interface from users. The next phase of Sekur's product roadmap is completing the new SekurOne, planned for release by the third week of December 2026, before Christmas, with SekurVoice expected to launch as a separate plan and additional new solutions expected to be launched at the same time. These launches are part of Sekur's preparation for 2027, as the Company has started pre-sales efforts in the U.S. and internationally.

Bringing SekurVoice into SekurMessenger means users can move from a secure chat to a secure voice call within the same application, with a cleaner layout and a more logical flow between functions. The redesign is intended to make everyday tasks quicker and more intuitive, so that users spend less time navigating the application and more time communicating.

The new interface changes how SekurMessenger looks and works for the user, not how it protects them. End-to-end encryption, self-destructing messages, encrypted file transfers, Chat-by-Invite, and Sekur ID identity management with no phone number required all remain in place, built on Sekur's proprietary, Swiss-hosted architecture with zero reliance on Big Tech cloud infrastructure.

"Security only works if people actually use it, and that means the experience has to be as easy as the everyday apps people are used to," said Alain Ghiai, Founder and CEO of Sekur Private Data. "The new SekurMessenger interface, with SekurVoice built in, makes secure messaging and calling simpler and faster, and the feedback we have received from users has been great."

"This is the first step in a broader refresh of the Sekur platform. Our next phase is completing the new SekurOne, which we plan to release by the third week of December, before Christmas, and we expect to unveil more than just SekurOne at that time, including SekurVoice as its own plan. We are also already working on new interfaces for our admin panel, our registration process, and SekurMail, so that every part of the Sekur experience, from sign-up to daily use, meets the same standard."

Next Phase: SekurOne, SekurVoice, and Additional Solutions Planned Before Christmas

With the new SekurMessenger UI deployed, Sekur's development focus now turns to completing the new SekurOne, its fully encrypted voice/video, email, messaging, and VPN platform engineered on the proprietary HeliX data transfer architecture. The new SekurOne is planned for release by the third week of December 2026, before Christmas.

SekurOne will not be launched alone. SekurVoice is expected to launch as a separate plan before Christmas, giving clients the option to subscribe to Sekur's encrypted voice calling on its own, and Sekur expects to launch additional new solutions at the same time, with the unveiling planned before Christmas. Further details will be announced at launch. The timing and content of these releases are subject to the completion of development and testing, and there can be no assurance that they will be released on that schedule.

Preparing for 2027: Pre-Sales Underway in the U.S. and Internationally

The new interfaces and December launches are intended to prepare Sekur for 2027. The Company has started pre-sales efforts in the U.S. and internationally, including Africa, Latin America, the Middle East, and Central and Eastern Europe, and plans to enter 2027 with a refreshed, easier-to-use platform and an expanded set of solutions to offer enterprise, government, defense, and executive clients in those markets. Pre-sales efforts may not result in sales, and there can be no assurance as to the timing or amount of any resulting revenue.

New Interfaces Underway for Admin Panel, Registration, and SekurMail

Sekur is also developing a new UI for its admin panel, which organizations use to manage their users and accounts; a new UI for its registration process, to make it simpler for new users and organizations to sign up and get started; and a new UI for its SekurMail solutions, the Company's secure business and executive email platform.

Together with the new SekurMessenger UI and the upcoming SekurOne, these updates are intended to give Sekur's enterprise, government, defense, and executive clients a consistent, user-friendly experience across the entire platform, from onboarding and administration to daily secure communications.

Sekur Core Communications Solutions

Sekur delivers secure communications that work within and beyond the Sekur network, operating independently of conventional telecom infrastructure to reduce exposure to interception, SIGINT collection, traffic analysis, metadata exploitation, and hostile surveillance in contested environments. No Sekur solution data-mines or location-tracks its users.

All solutions are built on proprietary architecture with zero reliance on Big Tech cloud infrastructure, meeting the privacy, security, and OPSEC requirements of intelligence agencies, defense and federal organizations, military commands, diplomatic missions, government agencies, executives, and professionals handling CUI and other sensitive, mission-critical information. Deployments are supported by on-premises infrastructure options for full data sovereignty, mission assurance, and sole control over keys and data.

SekurOne - Encrypted Voice/Video, Email, Messaging, and VPN

A fully encrypted communications platform engineered on proprietary HeliX data transfer architecture, purpose-built to defeat telecom network tracing, resist Pegasus-style malware intrusion, and support CUI handling requirements. SekurOne is designed for defense and federal officials, military commanders, government leaders, and executives conducting confidential, operational, or sensitive conversations where standard carrier-based voice and video platforms present unacceptable interception and exploitation risk.

Call-by-Invite capability via SMS or SekurSend email ensures controlled access and eliminates unsolicited contact. Each user is assigned a unique Sekur ID for identity management, with no phone number required - preserving user privacy across all voice and video communications.

SekurMail - Secure Business and Executive Email

An enterprise- and government-grade encrypted email platform designed for defense and federal agencies, military commands, senior government officials, C-suite executives, and organizations handling confidential and operationally sensitive communications, including CUI correspondence. Built on proprietary architecture with zero dependence on Big Tech cloud infrastructure and no metadata tracking, SekurMail keeps sensitive communications private between sender and recipient.

Key capabilities include SekurSend/SekurReply for secure delivery to non-Sekur recipients without exposing sender identity or message content; full message delivery control and audit capability; encrypted file transfer; custom domain support for organizational integration; and active protection against phishing, social engineering, and Business Email Compromise (BEC) attacks targeting corporate and administrative networks.

SekurMessenger - Secure Team Messaging and Collaboration

A secure messaging platform providing end-to-end encrypted text, file transfer, voice messages, and collaboration capabilities for defense, military, government, and executive teams coordinating operational and mission-sensitive information, including CUI material. Features include self-destructing messages, encrypted file transfers, and compliance-grade archiving for recordkeeping and audit requirements.

Cross-network secure communications with non-Sekur users are supported via Chat-by-Invite, enabling secure coordination with coalition partners, external agencies, and field elements without compromising the network. Each user is assigned a unique Sekur ID for identity verification and contact authentication, with no phone number required.

SekurVPN - Enterprise Network Security and Identity Protection

An enterprise-grade Virtual Private Network leveraging proprietary HeliX encryption technology, engineered to provide secure internet access, identity obfuscation, and traffic protection for defense organizations, military and federal personnel, government agencies, and executives operating across remote, traveling, deployed, forward, or untrusted network environments.

SekurVPN maintains zero data logging, ensuring no record of user activity exists that could be exposed through legal process, network compromise, or third-party collection. It is built for defense, government, and executive use cases - including protection of traffic associated with CUI and operationally sensitive workflows - where standard commercial VPN solutions present unacceptable privacy and security risk.

SekurRelay - Executive-Level Secure Email Integration

An enterprise-grade secure email relay solution enabling domain splitting, which allows organizations to establish secure communications at the executive, board, or senior staff level without requiring full organizational migration or infrastructure overhaul.

SekurRelay removes one of the most significant barriers to large-scale defense, government, and enterprise deployment, enabling phased adoption that protects command leadership, flag officers, and the highest-value personnel and communications immediately while broader organizational rollout proceeds. It is designed for defense and government organizations, regulated industries, and enterprises requiring rapid, low-friction elevation of communications security at the command and executive tier, including environments handling CUI communications.

About Sekur Private Data
Sekur Private Data is a Swiss-hosted cybersecurity, defense communications, and privacy solutions provider, offering a secure suite of tools to protect governments, defense and federal agencies, businesses, and individuals from unauthorized access and cyber threats. With capabilities such as SekurOne, SekurMail, SekurMessenger, and SekurVPN, Sekur provides a reliable and secure means of digital communication and data storage for Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI), classified-adjacent and civilian communications use, grounded in Swiss privacy standards with on-premises infrastructure for government agencies, allowing for data sovereignty. Sekur sells its solutions through its website www.sekur.com, approved distributors and telecommunications companies globally, and through the U.S. General Services Administration (GSA) Multiple Award Schedule (MAS), Contract No. 47QTCA18D0089 serving governments, defense institutions, federal agencies, businesses, and consumers worldwide. About NeuroSense

NeuroSense Therapeutics is a late-clinical stage biotechnology company developing novel treatments for severe neurodegenerative diseases, including amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) and Alzheimer's disease. The Company's lead product candidate, PrimeC, is a novel oral therapy designed to target multiple key biological pathways underlying disease progression, including neuroinflammation, oxidative stress and dysregulated iron metabolism.

NeuroSense has recently completed analysis of long-term follow-up data from its Phase 2b PARADIGM study in ALS, with results published in JAMA Neurology showing slowing of functional decline relative to placebo. The Company also reported changes across multiple biomarkers associated with ALS, including microRNAs, consistent with PrimeC's multi-target mechanism of action.

The Company has received clearance from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to initiate its pivotal Phase 3 PARAGON trial in ALS and is working with the FDA on an optimized study design.

About PrimeC

PrimeC, NeuroSense's lead drug candidate, is a novel extended-release oral formulation composed of a unique fixed-dose combination of two FDA-approved drugs: ciprofloxacin and celecoxib. PrimeC is designed to target several key mechanisms that contribute to neuron degeneration, inflammation, iron accumulation and impaired ribonucleic acid ("RNA") regulation, with the potential to inhibit disease progression.

Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis ("ALS") is an incurable neurodegenerative disease that causes complete paralysis and death within 3 years from diagnosis. Every year, more than 5,000 people are diagnosed with ALS in the U.S. alone, with an annual disease burden of $1 billion. The number of people living with ALS is expected to grow by 24% by 2040 in the U.S. and EU.

Key Terms

gaapfinancial
GAAP, or Generally Accepted Accounting Principles, are a set of standardized rules and guidelines that companies follow when preparing their financial statements. They ensure consistency, transparency, and comparability across different companies, making it easier for investors to understand and compare financial information accurately. This helps investors make informed decisions based on trustworthy and uniform financial reports.
View in glossary
vcseltechnical
A VCSEL is a tiny semiconductor laser that emits light straight out of the surface of a chip, like a miniature, very precise flashlight built into an electronic component. Investors care because VCSELs are key parts in optical communication, sensors, and proximity or gesture controls—products with growing demand—so changes in VCSEL supply, cost or adoption can affect a maker’s sales, margins and the competitive position of companies that rely on them.
accounts receivablefinancial
Money a company is owed by its customers for goods or services already delivered but not yet paid for. Think of it like a stack of IOUs or open tabs: it represents future cash the business expects to collect. Investors watch accounts receivable because large or growing balances can signal strong sales or potential cash shortfalls if customers don’t pay, affecting liquidity, working capital and the company’s financial health.
noncontrolling interestsfinancial
The portion of a subsidiary’s equity and profits that belongs to outside owners rather than the parent company; when a parent reports consolidated results it includes the whole subsidiary but shows the noncontrolling slice separately. Think of a company’s subsidiary as a pie where the parent owns most slices but some are held by other investors — noncontrolling interests tell you how much of the pie and its future earnings don’t belong to the parent, which affects how much profit and net assets are truly attributable to the parent’s shareholders.

("Cana"), in Athens, Greece. The first phase, comprising a new quality control laboratory and a new GMP warehouse, commences this quarter and is targeted for completion by the third quarter of 2027.

Strategic Rationale

Cana's contract manufacturing business continues to grow. Its contract manufacturing pipeline now exceeds 32.7 million units, Cana inaugurated a new capsule-filling production line in June 2026, and the Company recently announced the addition of an automated tablet coating system. The Master Plan is designed to ensure that Cana's infrastructure keeps pace with this growth and continues to meet applicable regulatory standards.

The program is structured across ten workstreams, each with defined deliverables, spanning engineering, permitting, construction, qualification and regulatory approval.

Phase One Scope and Timeline

  • Design and permitting (Q4 2026 - Q1 2027): engineering studies, architectural and structural design, and submission of the building permit application.
  • Quality control laboratory (Q1 - Q2 2027): construction of a new laboratory for quality control testing, followed by the transfer and qualification of laboratory instruments.
  • GMP warehouse (Q2 - Q3 2027): construction of a new warehouse in place of the existing warehouse, designed to improve the flow of materials into production, followed by qualification.
  • Regulatory inspection (Q3 2027): inspection by the EOF, targeted to complete the first phase.

Subsequent Phase

Following the first phase, the Master Plan provides for a dedicated powder production area within the facility. If completed and approved by the EOF, it would expand Cana's manufacturing portfolio with a purpose-built powder production capability, broadening the range of products available to contract manufacturing partners and to the Company's proprietary brands.

Greg Siokas, CEO of Cosmos Health, stated: "Our Facility Master Plan is designed to ensure that Cana's infrastructure keeps pace with the growth of its business. A new quality control laboratory and a new GMP warehouse form the foundation of the next stage of that growth, and we have a clear, structured plan in place, targeting completion by the third quarter of 2027.

NEW YORK CITY, NY / ACCESS Newswire / November 27, 2026 / The Age of Parity is no longer an abstract economic theory. It is becoming visible in real time.

A recent report in The New York Times examining the impact of surging fuel costs offers another reminder of how quickly an energy shock can become an economic shock. Recent fuel-price increases in Syria triggered widespread protests after diesel prices jumped 40 percent, while gasoline and other energy costs also increased sharply.

The circumstances in Syria are particular to that country. The larger economic lesson is not.

When oil becomes more expensive or difficult to obtain, the effects do not stop at the gas pump. They move through transportation, manufacturing, agriculture, packaging, logistics and eventually the price of everyday goods.

Plastic sits directly inside that equation.

Most conventional virgin plastic begins with fossil-fuel feedstocks. Its economics are therefore connected to a global system of oil and gas production, refining, transportation and trade. When that system becomes more expensive or unpredictable, manufacturers can feel the consequences far beyond the energy market.

That is why recycling plastic increasingly needs to be viewed as an economic strategy rather than simply an environmental objective.

SMX calls this shift the Age of Parity: the point at which the economics of recycled plastic begin competing more directly with the economics of virgin plastic.

For years, the conventional argument for recycling focused primarily on waste. Use less. Throw away less. Keep plastic out of landfills and oceans.

Those objectives remain important, but they no longer tell the whole story.

The economic argument may ultimately prove just as powerful.

Every tonne of usable plastic recovered from an existing waste stream represents material that potentially does not have to begin again with newly extracted fossil resources. Recycling creates the possibility of treating material already circulating through an economy as feedstock for the next generation of products.

That can turn waste into domestic inventory.

And in an era of volatile energy prices and disrupted supply chains, inventory matters.

THE NEW ECONOMICS OF PLASTIC

The Age of Parity changes the calculation because virgin plastic does not exist independently of the forces reshaping global energy markets.

Oil volatility and supply disruptions can affect the cost and availability of virgin material. Recycled plastic creates another potential supply source: material already contained in products, packaging and waste streams.

But for recycled plastic to function as a dependable industrial commodity, markets need more than supply. They need proof.

Manufacturers need to know what they are purchasing. Brands need evidence behind recycled-content claims. Regulators need information that can be audited. Buyers need a way to distinguish verified material from unsupported claims.

SMX's molecular marking and digital traceability technology is designed to give physical materials an identity that can remain connected to them through a supply chain. Molecular markers can be linked to digital records containing information about origin, composition and movement.

SMX's Digital Material Passport extends that identity into a digital record designed to travel with the material through its lifecycle. Instead of relying solely on paperwork or claims made at individual points in a supply chain, the passport is intended to connect physical plastic with information about what it is, where it came from and how it has moved through the system.

The company's Plastic Cycle Token (PCT)adds another component. It is designed to represent verified plastic-cycle activity digitally, connecting authenticated physical material with a tokenized record. Together, molecular identification, the Digital Material Passport and PCT are intended to create a bridge between physical recycling and the data needed to document it.

FROM WASTE STREAM TO SUPPLY STREAM

The Age of Parity reframes recycling from the final stop in a product's life to the beginning of another supply cycle.

Packaging, bottles, textiles and consumer products contain material that has already been manufactured. Recovering it does not eliminate the need for virgin plastic or insulate manufacturers from energy costs. It does create another potential source of raw material.

A manufacturer able to incorporate verified recycled material gains another procurement option. A country capable of recovering and reusing its plastic waste gains access to a material resource already within its borders.

The objective is not to declare recycled plastic universally cheaper than virgin plastic. Prices vary by polymer, geography, energy costs, processing requirements and market conditions. The larger change is that recycled plastic can increasingly be evaluated as an industrial input rather than simply an environmental substitute.

THE MATERIAL IS ALREADY HERE

Plastic presents an unusual opportunity because so much potential raw material is already in circulation. The question is whether economies can capture, identify and reuse it.

Technology alone cannot accomplish that. Collection systems, recycling infrastructure, manufacturers, regulators and markets all have roles to play. SMX's role is focused on identity and verification: connecting physical material with a record intended to remain useful as that material moves through successive cycles.

That matters because circularity ultimately depends on knowing what came back.

Plastic that can be recovered, identified, verified and reused is not merely waste diverted from a landfill. It is a resource that does not have to be created from scratch.

That is what the Age of Parity ultimately represents: not the end of virgin plastic or oil, but the emergence of a competing model in which yesterday's products can become tomorrow's raw materials.

In a world being reminded how quickly resource prices can change, throwing that material away is becoming increasingly difficult to justify.

ABOUT SMX (SECURITY MATTERS) PLC

SMX (Security Matters) PLC (NASDAQ:SMX) develops molecular traceability and material authentication technologies designed to strengthen supply-chain transparency and integrity across global industries. Its platform embeds invisible molecular markers directly into physical materials-including solids, liquids, and gases-allowing them to carry a persistent identity that can be detected and verified throughout their lifecycle.

Toronto, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - November 27, 2026) - Nickel 28 Capital Corp. (TSXV: NKL) (FSE: 3JC0) ("Nickel 28" or the "Company") is pleased to provide operational results for the calendar quarter ending September 30, 2026 for the Company's largest asset, the Ramu Nickel-Cobalt ("Ramu") integrated operation in Papua New Guinea. Production, shipment and inventory figures are reported on a 100% Ramu basis. Nickel 28 currently holds an 8.56% joint-venture interest in Ramu which is operated by the Metallurgical Corporation of China ("MCC").

Q3 2026 Ramu Highlights:

  • Production of 9,043 tonnes of contained nickel in Mixed Hydroxide Precipitate ("MHP"), compared to 9,242 tonnes in the same period last year.
  • Production of 929 tonnes of contained cobalt in MHP, compared to 887 tonnes in the same period last year.
  • Nickel sales of 7,403 tonnes of contained nickel, compared to 9,880 tonnes in the same period last year.
  • Cobalt sales of 775 tonnes of contained cobalt, compared to 948 tonnes in the same period last year.
  • Nickel inventory on hand at quarter-end was 2,734 tonnes of nickel in MHP, compared to 1,094 tonnes at June 30, 2026.
  • London Metal Exchange average nickel price of US$7.52/lb in Q3 2026, an increase of 10% from the same period last year (US$6.81/lb).
  • Average cobalt price of US$24.41/lb in Q3 2026, an increase of 58% from the same period last year (US$15.48/lb).
  • Production costs, net of by-product credits were US$6.15/lb of nickel produced in MHP, compared to US$3.07/lb in the same period last year, primarily reflecting higher sulphur prices. Year-to-date 2026 production costs, net of by-product credits, were US$4.25/lb of nickel produced in MHP, compared to US$3.27/lb in the same period last year.

Nickel 28's Chief Executive Officer, Craig Lennon stated: "Ramu continued to deliver strong operational performance during the third quarter of 2026, with nickel and cobalt production remaining robust and the project continuing to demonstrate its operational reliability. While reported sales volumes were lower than the previous quarter, this was principally attributable to the timing of a shipment that was not recognised within the quarter. As a result, inventory levels increased at quarter end, and we expect this timing difference to reverse in the following quarter. Importantly, the lower sales volumes do not reflect any deterioration in underlying production performance.

The operating environment has, however, become increasingly challenging, with a significant increase in production costs during the quarter, driven primarily by the continued escalation in sulphur prices. Sulphur is a major consumable in the high-pressure acid leach (HPAL) process, and the sustained increase in its price has had a material impact on operating costs and margins. These cost pressures have been compounded by lower average nickel and cobalt prices during the quarter, resulting in a more difficult financial environment than we experienced during the first half of 2026.

Nickel prices softened during the quarter, reflecting continued concerns regarding global oversupply, particularly from Indonesia. Cobalt prices also weakened as increased availability of material from the Democratic Republic of Congo and subdued downstream demand placed pressure on the market. The combination of lower commodity prices and higher input costs has resulted in a significant compression of operating margins, despite the continued strong production performance at Ramu.

Looking ahead, Indonesian governmental policy remains a critical factor in determining the direction of global nickel prices. In particular, the Indonesian government's management of nickel ore production quotas through its Work Plan and Budget (Rencana Kerja dan Anggaran Biaya, or RKAB) approval process will be closely watched by the industry. The RKAB is the mandatory annual operational and financial blueprint that mining license holders must get approved by the Indonesian Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources or relevant local governor before carrying out exploration or production activities. Recent indications that Indonesia may adopt a more restrictive approach to production quotas in 2027 are encouraging and could help address the current global supply imbalance. However, the extent and timing of any resulting improvement in nickel prices remain uncertain.

While we remain confident in the underlying operational performance of Ramu, we expect the challenging cost and commodity price environment to continue to impact profitability and cash generation in the near term. The focus for the project remains on maintaining strong production performance, managing operating costs where possible and positioning the project to benefit from any improvement in market conditions."

LOS ANGELES--(BUSINESS WIRE)--

Faraday Future Intelligent Electric Inc. (NASDAQ: FFAI) (“Faraday Future”, “FF” or the “Company”), a California-based global Embodied AI (EAI) ecosystem company, today highlighted a significant milestone in its development as a Physical AI investment holding company. FF EAI Robotics Ecosystem Inc. (NASDAQ: FFR) (“FFR”) filed a preliminary Schedule 14C with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC”) on November 25, marking the completion of all material matters required of both parties post deal closing. Following completion of the relevant procedures and assuming the issuances described in the filing, FFAI is expected to hold approximately 75% of FFR’s outstanding common stock. Based on FFR’s closing share price on November 25, the implied value of this expected ownership position would be approximately $41 million.

Faraday Future Highlights Expected FFR Equity Position Valued at Approximately $41 Million, Offering FFAI Stockholders Participation in FFR’s Potential Long-Term Value Creation

As previously announced, the robotics business incubated by FFAI was combined into FFR on October 23, 2026. The transaction gives the robotics business room to develop independently. The robotics business will use FFR as a standalone platform for financing and accounting, which will make its performance more transparent and help investors manage a closed loop from investment to results.

FFAI’s expected ownership position represents a significant milestone for its future development and provides FFAI stockholders with an opportunity to participate in FFR’s potentially substantial future value creation and returns. It also reinforces Faraday Future’s long-term commitment to the robotics business it incubated, as FFR advances its technologies, products, strategic partnerships and commercialization initiatives. As of November 25, 2026, FFAI beneficially held approximately 14.7 million shares of FFR common stock, representing approximately 53% of outstanding common shares. Assuming all issuances under the Nasdaq Issuance Proposal described in FFR’s preliminary information statement, excluding shares issuable upon exercise of assumed options, FFAI would hold approximately 80.1 million common shares, representing approximately 75% of the resulting outstanding common stock of FFR. All newly issued FFR shares received by FFAI in the transaction are subject to an 18-month lock-up period.

The implied value would be approximately $41 million and is based on that expected ownership position and FFR’s November 25 closing share price. It remains subject to market-price fluctuations and completion of the applicable conversion and issuance procedures.

“This milestone highlights the potential value of our ownership position in FFR and its importance to FFAI’s future development,” said YT Jia, Founder and Global CEO of FF and FFR. “Through our continued participation in FFR, FFAI stockholders have an opportunity to share in the potential long-term value created by the robotics business we incubated. We believe FFR’s growing portfolio of technologies, products, partnerships and commercialization initiatives can create substantial opportunities as the Physical AI industry develops.”

Faraday Future recently announced a strategic upgrade toward becoming a Physical AI investment holding company and a Robotaxi and AI VisiCabin shared-mobility operations company. Under this strategy, FFAI aims to build its Physical AI investment portfolio through strategic investments, acquisitions and ecosystem development, while evolving its automotive business toward a lighter-asset model focused on shared-mobility operations and intelligent cabin technologies. Its substantial ownership position in FFR is a key component of this strategy, providing continued participation in the potential growth of the robotics business it incubated and an opportunity to create long-term value for FFAI stockholders. FFR is building a “Four-Core Full-Stack AI” ecosystem encompassing the Physical AI Brain and Developer Platform, Physical AI Devices, Industry Productivity Solutions and Physical AI Data Factory. Its commercialization efforts span education and research, security and inspection, industrial and other enterprise applications.

Key Terms

schedule 14cregulatory
Schedule 14C is an SEC filing that companies use to send an official information statement to shareholders when they are not asking for proxy votes. It lays out key facts about corporate actions—such as reorganizations, related-party transactions, or changes in governance—so investors can understand what’s happening without being asked to vote, like receiving a detailed neighborhood notice about a rule change rather than a petition. Because it provides formal, regulated disclosure, Schedule 14C helps investors verify claims, weigh potential impacts on ownership or value, and hold management accountable.
lock-up periodfinancial
A lock-up period is a fixed time after a stock offering during which company insiders and early investors are legally barred from selling their shares. It matters because when that restriction expires a large block of previously locked-up shares can enter the market at once, potentially lowering the stock price or spiking trading volume—like opening a floodgate—so investors monitor these dates to anticipate price moves and manage risk.

Salt Lake City, Utah, Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- TruGolf Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ: TRUG), today announced a 1-for-5 reverse split of its Class A common stock. The reverse stock split was approved by the Company’s Board of Directors in accordance with Section 78.207 of the Nevada Revised Statutes and is intended to enable the Company to regain compliance with the $1.00 minimum bid price requirement for continued listing on The Nasdaq Capital Market. Beginning on December 1, 2026, the Company’s Class A common stock will continue to trade on The Nasdaq Capital Market on a split adjusted basis under the trading symbol “TRUG” but will trade under the following new CUSIP number: 243733706.

As a result of the reverse stock split, every 5 shares of Class A common stock issued and outstanding as of the effective date will be automatically combined into one share of Class A common stock. No fractional shares will be issued if, as a result of the reverse stock split, a stockholder would otherwise become entitled to a fractional share because the number of shares of Class A common stock they hold before the reverse stock split is not evenly divisible by the split ratio. Instead, each stockholder will be entitled to receive a cash payment in lieu of a fractional share.

The reverse stock split will reduce the number of shares of outstanding Class A common stock from approximately 2.9 million shares, the number of shares outstanding as of the date hereof, to approximately 0.57 million shares. The par value of the Class A common stock will remain unchanged and the number of authorized shares of Class A common stock will be proportionately reduced to 2 million shares. The reverse split affects all stockholders uniformly and will not alter any common stockholder’s percentage interest in the Company’s equity, except to the extent that the reverse split results in some common stockholders owning a fractional share as described above.

About TruGolf

TruGolf Holdings (NASDAQ: TRUG) is where the consumer technology of TruGolf meets the institutional finance of Polymath. The Company is well positioned in tokenized finance while operating and growing a real technology business. Polymath develops enterprise-grade capital markets infrastructure for the issuance, compliance, and lifecycle management of regulated digital securities and other tokenized financial instruments. It enables issuers, investors, and market participants to create and manage tokenized representations of real-world assets within compliant frameworks, supporting investor onboarding, regulatory controls, and post-issuance administration across private and institutional markets. TruGolf is recognized as a leader in the golf simulator market, manufacturing and distributing cutting-edge software and hardware that redefines what is possible with golf technology. Its products are designed to capture the spirit of golf, blending tradition with modern innovation. Combined, these two businesses are well positioned in distinct growing markets but sharing the costs of one listed company. This is the power and potential of two digital native businesses working together.
